raw_response:
Well, let me think about this year the way I always do.

I'm getting on now — 63, and with just myself in the house, I can't do everything by hand anymore. My boy's working in the city, and my wife passed some years back. So for the busy times — wheat harvest, maize planting, maize harvest — I pay the fellow down the road with the combine. Costs me money but I got no choice. On 16 mu I can manage the rest myself if I take it slow.

**The wheat** — I put that in back in October like always. Before planting I spread about 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu, that's what I've done for years and my neighbor Old Liu does about the same. Now it's spring, the wheat is greening up. When it starts jointing I'll topdress some urea, maybe one bag per mu, and run the well water. Wheat needs the water at jointing and again when it's heading, otherwise the grain don't fill. Last year I watered three times and got about 420 kg per mu — pretty good. I'll do the same.

**The maize** — soon as the wheat comes off in June I got to turn around fast and get the maize in. No time to plow proper, I hire the no-till planter that goes right through the stubble. For maize I use a hybrid seed from the agro-shop in town, the same kind most folks around here buy — Zhengdan or one of those. Put down compound fertilizer with the seed, then topdress urea when it's knee-high. If summer rains come good I might not irrigate at all; if it's dry I'll water once or twice.

I don't like to spend more than I have to. Fertilizer prices been high, but if you skimp too much the yield drops and then you're worse off. Better put a little extra than not enough — that's what 25 years taught me. For weeds I spray herbicide myself, it's not hard. Pests on maize I usually don't need to spray unless the borer gets bad.
